criteria.quote: "A peck fails. A tip spills Metapod's insides."
criteria.revision: Open on the unresolved contrast instead: "Pikipek can't crack Metapod's shell—so why does Metapod barely move?" Save the spilling reveal for the later tip-over scene.

criteria.quote: "Pikipek pecks its shell, but the shell does not crack."
"Why does Metapod stay still if its shell already stops Pikipek?"
criteria.revision: Do not answer the question in scene one. Replace its narration with the open-loop wording, then reveal that Metapod risks spilling its innards only after establishing its hard shell and soft interior.

criteria.quote: "A peck fails. A tip spills Metapod's insides." / "The shell survives pecks, but tipping can spill Metapod out."
criteria.revision: Remove the tip-and-spill result from scene one and reserve it for scene five. Build from the failed peck, to the tender innards, to Metapod's motionlessness, then reveal that tipping it over can spill its insides.

Hide the central reversal until the reveal: make scene one about the shell resisting Pikipek, then let "it will tip over, spilling out its insides" be the first explicit statement of the strange weakness.

criteria.quote: "A peck fails. A tip spills Metapod's insides." / "Pikipek pecks its shell, but the shell does not crack." / "The shell survives pecks, but tipping can spill Metapod out."
criteria.revision: Give each beat one job: scene one asks why it stays still, scene two proves Pikipek cannot crack the shell, scene three establishes its soft innards, scene four establishes the risk of spilling them, and scene five delivers the tip-over fact once.

criteria.quote: "Metapod’s shell is strong, but staying still protects the soft innards that could spill when it tips."
criteria.revision: Make the payoff explicitly answer the opening contrast: "Pikipek's pecks aren't what Metapod has to fear: even with an uncracked shell, tipping over can spill its soft insides."

criteria.quote: "Trust Metapod’s hard shell, or avoid intense battles with it?"
criteria.revision: Replace the false practical choice with a credible interpretation split grounded in the reveal: "Does Pikipek failing to crack the shell make Metapod seem safe—or does the fact it can tip over and spill its insides change everything?"
